prerequisites: Meeting the enrolment conditions for the Master's study programme of Mechanical Engineering
Passing grade for exercises and other individual assignments.

learning_outcomes.text: The student knows and understands the content and mission of a smart factory compared to traditional factories.
Acquired knowledge is used by the student to draft and design processes in smart factories and to integrate them into the whole concept of a smart factory.
Acquired knowledge is used by the student to make effective use of Industry 4.0 technologies in a smart factory.
Acquired knowledge is used by the student to produce digital twins of processes and the entire smart factory, as well as to control the whole system.
To learn about key technologies of Industry 4.0 and the concept of distributed systems.
Knows and understands how to use tools to evaluate the status of digitization of a traditional factory.
Knows and understands how to use computer-aided tools for drafting an efficient smart factory for various purposes.
Recognize the usefulness of Industry 4.0 technologies in a smart factory.
Knows and understands how to use simulation tools for building a digital twin of a smart factory with different subprocesses.

syllabus_topics: Smart factories and their definitions, concepts and development approaches
Disciplines, systems and technologies related to Industry 4.0
Referential architectural models of smart factories and concept of distributed systems
Top-down and bottom-up approach when implementing solutions of Industry 4.0
The concept of digital twins (DT) of manufacturing processes of a smart factory
Five-dimensional modelling of a DT and its key technologies
Control of a smart production with a digital twin
Advanced production systems integration into a smart factory

assessment_methods.method: Colloquium, team work presentation/defence, writing and/or oral exam (theoretical contents)
Individual work in exercises, individual laboratory work (including reports)

assessment_rules: The final grade is composed of 50% theoretical content (colloquium, team work presentation/defense, writing and/or oral exam) and 50% individual work in exercises and laboratory work (including reports).
